Faith or Deity:
The Radiant Concord, a religious tradition teaching that light is a public
trust. Knowledge, aid, judgment, and authority should be made visible and
directed toward the protection of the community.

The Concord has no single universally recognized deity. Some congregations
name a divine source; others teach that disciplined public service is itself
the sacred flame.

Religious Office or Former Role:
Public liturgist and relief clerk at the House of the Open Lantern.

Deep umber-brown skin.

Hair, Crest, Horns, or Other Distinguishing Features:
Dense, tightly curled black hair worn in a rounded shoulder-length shape;
sharply pointed ears; elegant, expressive features.

Eyes:
Very dark brown, nearly black, with faint gold flecks.

General Appearance:
A tall, dark-skinned Wood Elf with fine-boned features, an expressive face,
and the poised bearing of a practiced public performer. Her gestures are
controlled but lively, and her presence is difficult to ignore.

She wears an acolyte robe while traveling and keeps a set of fine clothes for
formal appearances. A clear crystal serves as her Sorcerer spellcasting focus.
Her holy symbol is a small brass lamp with open shutters.

FEATURES AND ABILITIES

Class Features:

Spellcasting
Sorcerer 1 casts Sorcerer spells using Charisma. Her spell save DC is 13 and
her spell attack bonus is +5. She can use an Arcane Focus for Sorcerer spells.

Innate Sorcery
Twice per Long Rest, Sorcerer 1 can activate Innate Sorcery as a Bonus Action
for 1 minute. During that time, the spell save DC of her Sorcerer spells
increases by 1, and she has Advantage on attack rolls for Sorcerer spells.


Subclass Features:

None at level 1. Sorcerer subclass is chosen at level 3.


Species Traits:

Source-Rules Combination
The source character combines a 2024 Sorcerer class and Acolyte background with
the older Wood Elf trait package printed on the character sheet. This record
preserves the source traits rather than silently replacing them.

Darkvision
Sorcerer 1 has Darkvision to 60 ft.

Keen Senses
Sorcerer 1 is proficient in Perception.

Fey Ancestry
Sorcerer 1 has Advantage on saving throws against being Charmed, and magic
cannot put her to sleep.

Trance
Sorcerer 1 does not need to sleep. She normally completes a Long Rest by
meditating semiconsciously for 4 hours.

Elf Weapon Training
Sorcerer 1 is trained with Longsword, Shortsword, Shortbow, and Longbow. The
source proficiency summary omits Shortbow, but the full trait text includes it.

Fleet of Foot
Sorcerer 1's walking Speed is 35 ft.

Mask of the Wild
Sorcerer 1 can attempt to Hide while only lightly obscured by qualifying
natural phenomena.

Sorcerer 1 knows Thaumaturgy and Mending and always has Healing Word prepared.
Charisma is the spellcasting ability for these spells. Healing Word can be
cast once without a spell slot per Long Rest and can also be cast using
Sorcerer spell slots.

PERSONALITY TRAITS

Sorcerer 1 has persistent doubts about whether other people overestimate her
competence, especially when they look to her for an answer in a difficult
situation.

She has persistent imposter syndrome. She expects the moment when everyone
realizes that they have overestimated her, even though she consistently makes
sound decisions, communicates clearly, notices what a group needs, and earns
confidence.

Her discomfort has no obvious external cause. It exists almost entirely
between her own ears.

She is more capable than she believes herself to be. She listens, weighs the
available information, accepts responsibility, and can make a firm choice when
hesitation would be dangerous.

Her private wish is to become First Flame of the Radiant Concord one day. She
would love for it to happen, but she does not regard it as a realistic plan.
The idea feels more like an impossible dream than a career she expects to
complete.

Knitting is her regular hobby rather than a decorative biographical detail.
Whenever there is usable downtime, she takes out her current project and
continues working.

She makes well-crafted hats, scarves, and mittens. When her traveling group reaches a
town, she sells the finished pieces to merchants and begins another project.

She is entirely comfortable knitting during serious discussions, planning
sessions, long watches, wagon rides, meals, and arguments about urgent threats.
The activity helps her think and does not mean she has stopped listening.

Sorcerer 1 has a formidable sweet tooth and very little restraint once a sweet
food clearly belongs to her. She will not steal from a shop, raid another
person's plate, or treat unattended pastries as free property.

The danger begins when the sweets are hers. If someone gives her twelve
muffins as a gift, she is entirely capable of eating all twelve in one sitting.

She therefore discourages people from giving her large gifts of cakes,
candies, sweet rolls, preserved fruit, or similar food. Keeping the gift for
later is much harder than declining it in the first place.

Sorcerer 1 spent roughly the first seventy years of her life in an isolated
Wood Elf community that distrusted outsiders, took intense pride in its own
customs, and treated the wider world as corrupt, foolish, or dangerous.

She later entered the House of the Open Lantern and learned its local rituals,
records, relief work, and civic procedures. That education did not teach her
how the broader world works.

She is naive about ordinary customs outside the few societies she knows. She
may understand a difficult ritual or relief ledger while remaining baffled by
a common urban convenience, a widely recognized institution, a familiar piece
of slang, or a social expectation that everyone else assumes requires no
explanation.

This ignorance is practical rather than childlike. She is not foolish, and she
can learn quickly once something is explained. She simply lacks the enormous
body of everyday knowledge most travelers accumulate without noticing.

IDEALS

Power.

Sorcerer 1 privately dreams of becoming First Flame, the highest governing
office of the Radiant Concord.

She does not expect the dream to come true. Even leading four companions feels
like a role she was accidentally given and may eventually be exposed as
unqualified to hold.

She believes charitable institutions fail when people with weak judgment,
divided responsibility, or private interests control their resources. In her
view, good intentions without sufficient authority are easily ignored.

If she ever possessed real institutional power, she would want the Concord's
relief houses, schools, storehouses, and public records to answer to one
visible standard.

The desire is genuine. The confidence required to pursue it is not.

Source Roll:
Acolyte Ideal d6 result 4.

BONDS

Sorcerer 1 will do anything necessary to protect the House of the Open Lantern.

The House raised and trained her, gave her a public voice, and taught her how
food, medicine, petitions, records, and ritual can hold a town together.

Its relief stores were among the supplies diverted through the Storehouse of
Quiet Accounts. Its seal was copied and used on false transfer orders.

Source Roll:
Acolyte Bond d6 result 5.

FLAWS

Sorcerer 1 is suspicious of strangers and expects the worst of them.

A person without references, a traveler with an incomplete story, an official
whose seal she does not recognize, or a newcomer asking detailed questions
about supplies immediately attracts her scrutiny.

The theft from the House of the Open Lantern proved some of her suspicions
correct, making the flaw harder to challenge.

She may identify genuine danger early. She may also treat an innocent person
as guilty because caution feels more responsible than trust.

Source Roll:
Acolyte Flaw d6 result 5.

ALLIES AND ORGANIZATIONS

Name or Group:
The Radiant Concord

Relationship or Connection:
Sorcerer 1's faith and the hierarchy she privately dreams of leading

Notes:
The Concord operates temples, schools, relief counters, public lamps,
petition halls, and supply houses.

Name or Group:
The House of the Open Lantern

Relationship or Connection:
Sorcerer 1's temple, former home, and protected institution

Notes:
The House serves as shrine, public meeting hall, writing office, relief depot,
and place of temporary refuge.

Someone copied its seal and redirected part of its winter supply allocation
through false civic records.

Name or Group:
The Chamber of Seven Flames

Relationship or Connection:
Regional governing council of the Radiant Concord and object of Sorcerer 1's
most improbable private ambition

Notes:
The Chamber appoints temple heads, audits major storehouses, recognizes
doctrinal rulings, and controls the distribution of emergency funds.

Sorcerer 1 would love to enter the Chamber and become its First Flame. She
does not believe she is likely to do either.

Several members benefited politically from the centralized transfer system
that allowed the thefts to remain hidden.

Supporting Organization Roll:
d20 result 15.

Name or Group:
Luminary Sera Venn

Relationship or Connection:
Former instructor, current temple superior, and first institutional sponsor

Notes:
Sera trained Sorcerer 1 in public liturgy, petition hearings, relief records,
and the controlled use of a commanding voice.

She encouraged Sorcerer 1's ambition while repeatedly warning that certainty
and wisdom are not the same thing.

Sera remained at the House of the Open Lantern after the storehouse thefts.
Her current health, freedom, and political position are uncertain.

Supporting Relationship Roll:
d20 result 5.

CHARACTER NOTES, GOALS, FEARS, AND RELATIONSHIPS

Goals:

Sorcerer 1 wants to recover the original Open Lantern transfer ledger and the
seal plate used to create false orders.

The missing ledger would identify which officials authorized the rerouting of
temple, military, and public-relief supplies.

She wants enough standing within the Radiant Concord that officials cannot
dismiss the evidence or bury the investigation.

In her most private moments, she imagines becoming First Flame and replacing
the fragmented transfer system with a single public chain of responsibility.
She treats that future as a wish, not an attainable plan.

Supporting Goal Roll:
d20 result 10.

Fears:

Sorcerer 1 fears that her magic is not a blessing from the Radiant Concord.

Her power appeared during a public rite and was immediately interpreted by
witnesses as a sacred sign. That interpretation gave her status, training,
and a path toward authority.

She has never received proof that the Concord caused, chose, or understands
her sorcery.

She fears that the power may be accidental, inherited, or connected to
something the faith would condemn. More personally, she fears that she accepted
the language of divine selection because it served her ambition.

Supporting Fear Roll:
d20 result 3.

Habits or Mannerisms:

Before giving an important order, she briefly checks the faces of the others
as though expecting someone more qualified to interrupt.

She asks for advice sincerely, but once a decision is required, she can become
surprisingly calm and definite.

She carries a knitting project during travel and produces it whenever the
group stops long enough for her hands to be free.

Her usual projects are hats, scarves, and mittens made neatly enough to sell.
She keeps finished pieces packed until her traveling group reaches a town, then sells
them to an interested merchant.

She commonly knits through tactical discussions, investigations, arguments,
and decisions about major threats. When someone objects that she is knitting
during an important conversation, she answers that she can multitask.

She does not need silence to knit and does not treat the activity as withdrawal
from the group. She keeps listening, asks questions, offers opinions, and makes
decisions while her hands continue working.

She does not habitually make comic, sentimental, or personalized gifts for her
companions. Her knitting is a private hobby and a modest source of ordinary trade.

She refuses large gifts of sweets with unusual intensity. If pressed, she may
say, “Do not make them mine.”

Once sweet food has been explicitly given to her, she divides it into portions
with excellent intentions and then steadily eats every portion.

She frequently asks what an unfamiliar custom, institution, object, phrase, or
piece of etiquette is for. Her questions may concern things so commonplace
that companions initially assume she is joking.

When someone says, “Everyone knows that,” she answers, quite seriously, “I
didn't.”

She compares unfamiliar practices to the customs of her forest community or
the House of the Open Lantern, often without realizing how narrow those two
points of reference are.

She can conceal embarrassment behind a persuasive explanation, but her ears
and posture usually reveal when the wider world has surprised her.

Important Relationships:

The House of the Open Lantern:
Her former home and the institution she will do anything to protect.

The Chamber of Seven Flames:
The governing council she secretly wishes she could join and ultimately lead,
despite believing the ambition is beyond her.

The Radiant Concord:
Her faith, source of identity, instrument of public service, and intended path
to power.

Other Character Notes:

Her sweet-tooth problem applies to sweets she understands to be hers. It does
not compel theft, trespass, taking another person's food, or ignoring an
explicit prohibition.

Her unfamiliarity with the wider world reflects an isolated upbringing and
limited experience, not an inability to learn.

Her finished hats, scarves, and mittens are ordinary, well-made trade goods.
She sells them to merchants in town. They are not automatic gifts for her
companions, do not create special bonds or comic costumes, and provide only whatever
ordinary payment a buyer agrees to offer.

Her Intelligence 8 does not prevent spellcasting because Sorcerer magic and
Magic Initiate use Charisma. It does affect Intelligence checks and reflects
the source character's recorded abilities.

The source character uses legacy Wood Elf traits alongside 2024 class and
background rules. Those traits are preserved as printed.

The duplicate source entry for two additional oil flasks has been removed.
Sorcerer 1 carries two oil flasks total.

The nightmarish idol affects creatures that sleep near it. Sorcerer 1 normally
Trances rather than sleeping. The idol grants no combat benefit, spell effect,
or control over dreams.

The false temple seal, missing transfer ledger, Chamber of Seven Flames,
Luminary Sera Venn, and uncertain source of Sorcerer 1's magic are future story
hooks.

FORMATIVE EVENT

Sorcerer 1's formative event was the Rite of Uncovered Flame.

During a crowded public ceremony at the House of the Open Lantern, she was
assigned to read the names of households receiving winter aid.

A regional official interrupted the rite and announced that several
allocations had been suspended pending review. Sorcerer 1 challenged the
decision in front of the congregation.

As her voice rose, every lamp in the hall flared at once. Colored sparks moved
through the air around her hands, the crystal on the central lectern cracked,
and her words carried through the entire building without effort.

No one was seriously harmed.

The congregation treated the event as a sign that the Radiant Concord had
marked her for greater service. Luminary Sera Venn arranged training and
placed the clear half of the cracked crystal in Sorcerer 1's care.

The incident transformed her from a promising acolyte into a public figure.
It also connected her ambition to a magical event whose origin remains
unproven.

Formative Event Roll:
d20 result 8.


BACKSTORY

Sorcerer 1 spent roughly the first seventy years of her life in a secluded
Wood Elf community deep within an old forest.

The community took great pride in its language, rituals, memory, craft, and
relationship with the surrounding land. It also treated outsiders with deep
suspicion and taught that most other societies were noisy, corrupt, hurried,
and spiritually careless.

Sorcerer 1 eventually left and settled near the House of the Open Lantern in a
prosperous town whose markets, workshops, shrines, patrol posts, schools, and
warehouses all depended upon shared records.

The transition taught her the workings of one temple and one town. It did not
give her a broad education in the customs, institutions, technology, slang,
and assumptions of the wider world.

She entered the Radiant Concord as an adult and discovered that she had a
natural presence in public space.

She guided responses during ceremonies, read petitions aloud, copied relief
orders, prepared seals, and explained temple decisions to people who did not
have access to the officials making them.

Her strongest work was never private scholarship. It was standing before a
crowd, making an institution sound coherent, and persuading people that its
promises still mattered.

Luminary Sera Venn became her instructor.

Sera taught her that visible authority could protect vulnerable people, but
also that a confident voice could conceal weak reasoning. Sorcerer 1 absorbed
the first lesson more comfortably than the second.

The Rite of Uncovered Flame revealed her innate magic. The House interpreted
the event as divine recognition and arranged instruction in Sorcerer
spellcasting.

Sorcerer 1 also studied a small body of clerical magic through the Concord,
learning Thaumaturgy, Mending, and Healing Word.

Years later, the House discovered that part of its winter relief allocation
had never reached the listed villages.

The transfer records appeared correct. The seals appeared authentic.
Sorcerer 1 distrusted the civic officials who assured her that ordinary
accounting delays explained everything.

She followed differences in sealing wax, handwriting pressure, and delivery
dates to the Storehouse of Quiet Accounts.

Her investigation of the missing winter relief remains active. She wants enough
standing within the Radiant Concord that no one can dismiss that investigation
again. Far beyond that practical goal lies the private, nearly impossible wish
of becoming First Flame.

OPTIONAL BACKSTORY

This is optional story material only. It does not establish current party membership, leadership, or party role.

Sorcerer 1 followed irregularities in sealing wax, handwriting pressure, and delivery dates to the Storehouse of Quiet Accounts while investigating winter relief that had vanished from the House of the Open Lantern's records. Paladin 1 and Ranger 1, already partners from the same patrol service, were tracing missing military and public-relief supplies to the same building. Monk 1 entered separately as part of a Brass Ladder burglary. The investigations collided when Monk 1 abandoned his assigned route, discovered altered payment records, and triggered the storehouse alarms. His improvised path allowed the four to reach the central records room. Sorcerer 1 used magic to protect evidence and aid a wounded porter, Paladin 1 held the passage, and Ranger 1 secured surviving records and identified the route used to move the stolen goods. The four escaped with a torn ledger page, copied transfer marks, and proof that the theft extended beyond one temple, then continued traveling as the Town party.

Rule, Feature, Item, or Spell:
Mixed Wood Elf Rules Package

Full Effect:
The source character combines 2024 Sorcerer and Acolyte rules with an older
Wood Elf trait package. The record preserves Darkvision, Keen Senses, Fey
Ancestry, Trance, Elf Weapon Training, Fleet of Foot, and Mask of the Wild as
printed on the source sheet.

Source or Rules Reference:
Source D&D Beyond character sheet.


Rule, Feature, Item, or Spell:
The Radiant Concord, House of the Open Lantern, and Chamber of Seven Flames

Full Effect:
These institutions are part of Sorcerer 1's history and provide future
connections and conflicts. They grant no automatic shelter, authority,
supplies, money, information, votes, or institutional cooperation.

Source or Rules Reference:
WardensPC character material.


Rule, Feature, Item, or Spell:
Imposter Syndrome

Full Effect:
Sorcerer 1 doubts her right to lead despite performing the role well. This is
a personality trait and does not impose Disadvantage, reduce Charisma, alter
spellcasting, or prevent her from making decisions.

Source or Rules Reference:
WardensPC character material.


Rule, Feature, Item, or Spell:
Sweet Ownership Trigger

Full Effect:
Sorcerer 1 has poor restraint around sweet food that has clearly been given to
her or designated as hers.

This does not compel theft, trespass, taking another creature's food, consuming
unsafe substances, or ignoring direct orders. It is roleplaying guidance and
does not create a magical compulsion or automatic condition.

Source or Rules Reference:
WardensPC character material.


Rule, Feature, Item, or Spell:
Knitted Trade Goods

Full Effect:
Sorcerer 1 makes ordinary hats, scarves, and mittens during downtime and may
sell finished pieces to willing merchants.

The items are well made but grant no magical benefit. Sales use ordinary
negotiation and whatever price the buyer agrees to pay. Knitting does not
automatically generate money, bypass material costs, or produce a fixed amount
of goods during every rest.

The projects are not assumed to be gifts for the party.

Source or Rules Reference:
WardensPC character material.


Rule, Feature, Item, or Spell:
Nightmarish Idol

Full Effect:
A creature that sleeps near the idol experiences unsettling dreams. It grants
no combat effect, condition, damage, prophecy, information, or control over
dreams.

Sorcerer 1 normally completes a Long Rest through Trance rather than sleep.

feats_and_features: Spellcasting: Charisma-based Sorcerer spellcasting; clear crystal arcane focus. SRD rules: Drawing from your innate magic, you can cast spells. See “Spells” for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Sorcerer spells, which appear in the Sorcerer spell list later in the class’s description. Cantrips. You know four Sorcerer cantrips of your choice. Light, Prestidigitation, Shocking Grasp, and Sorcerous Burst are recommended. Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Sorcerer cantrip of your choice. When you reach Sorcerer levels 4 and 10, you learn another Sorcerer cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Sorcerer Features table. Spell Slots. The Sorcerer Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest. Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Sorcerer spells. Burning Hands and Detect Magic are recommended. The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Sorcerer levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Sorcerer Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Sorcerer spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Sorcerer Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you’re a level 3 Sorcerer, your list of prepared spells can include six Sorcerer spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination. If another Sorcerer feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don’t count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Sorcerer spells for you. Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you gain a Sorcerer level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Sorcerer spell for which you have spell slots. Spellcasting Ability. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Sorcerer spells. Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Sorcerer spells.

Innate Sorcery: Bonus Action; 2 uses per Long Rest; lasts 1 minute; Sorcerer spell save DC +1 and Advantage on Sorcerer spell attack rolls. Does not apply to Magic Initiate spells. SRD rules: An event in your past left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with simmering magic. As a Bonus Action, you can unleash that magic for 1 minute, during which you gain the following benefits:

Magic Initiate (Cleric): Thaumaturgy, Mending, and always-prepared Healing Word using Charisma; Healing Word has one free Long Rest casting and can also use Sorcerer spell slots. SRD rules: Origin Feat. You gain the following benefits. Two Cantrips. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Cleric, Druid, or Wizard spell list. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat’s spells (choose when you select this feat). Level 1 Spell. Choose a level 1 spell from the same list you selected for this feat’s cantrips. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have. Spell Change. Whenever you gain a new level, you can replace one of the spells you chose for this feat with a different spell of the same level from the chosen spell list. Repeatable. You can take this feat more than once, but you must choose a different spell list each time.
Acolyte: Insight, Religion, and Calligrapher's Supplies proficiency; ability score increases already applied.
Keen Senses: Perception proficiency. SRD rules: You have proficiency in the Insight, Perception, or Survival skill.
Fey Ancestry: Advantage on saves against being Charmed; magic cannot put her to sleep. SRD rules: You have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Charmed condition.

Trance: does not need sleep and normally Long Rests through 4 hours of semiconscious meditation. SRD rules: You don’t need to sleep, and magic can’t put you to sleep. You can finish a Long Rest in 4 hours if you spend those hours in a trancelike meditation, during which you retain consciousness.
Elf Weapon Training: Longsword, Shortsword, Shortbow, and Longbow training.
Fleet of Foot: walking Speed 35 ft.
Mask of the Wild: may attempt to Hide while lightly obscured by qualifying natural phenomena.
Weapon proficiencies: simple weapons, longsword, shortsword, shortbow, and longbow.
No armor training, shield training, subclass, Weapon Mastery feature, or attuned items.

story_facts.fact: She is a public liturgist and relief clerk formerly attached to the House of the Open Lantern, a shrine, meeting hall, writing office, relief depot, and refuge.
Her faith, the Radiant Concord, teaches that light is a public trust: knowledge, aid, judgment, and authority should visibly protect the community. It has no single universally recognized deity.
She was raised for roughly seventy years in an isolated Wood Elf community that distrusted outsiders and regarded broader society as corrupt, foolish, or dangerous.
She is practically naive about many customs, institutions, slang terms, and expectations outside her forest community and the House of the Open Lantern, but learns quickly when matters are explained.
Her innate magic emerged at the Rite of Uncovered Flame, when lamps flared, sparks gathered around her hands, a lectern crystal cracked, and her voice carried through the hall.
Luminary Sera Venn gave her the clear half of the cracked crystal now used as her Sorcerer focus.
The House of the Open Lantern's relief stores were diverted through the Storehouse of Quiet Accounts using copied seals and false transfer orders.

She seeks the original Open Lantern transfer ledger and the seal plate used to create false orders, which could identify officials responsible for rerouting temple, military, and public-relief supplies.
Several Chamber of Seven Flames members benefited politically from the centralized transfer system that allowed the thefts to remain hidden.
Luminary Sera Venn remains at the House of the Open Lantern, but her health, freedom, and political position are uncertain.
She fears her sorcery may not be a blessing of the Radiant Concord and may instead be accidental, inherited, or tied to something her faith would condemn.
Her private ambition is to join the Chamber of Seven Flames and become First Flame, though she considers that dream nearly impossible.
The nightmarish idol causes unsettling dreams for creatures that sleep near it. Sorcerer 1 normally Trances rather than sleeping, and it has no combat, prophetic, or controlling effect.
